first_impression.reaction: Paros. I hadn't heard much about it, which I'll take as a good sign after Mykonos. The opening is plain and sensible: three parts of the island, and it depends on numbers, the ceremony and whether everyone sleeps under one roof. That last bit is exactly what I'd be thinking about. I'll read it properly.

journey.quote: The Municipality of Paros runs a civil marriages section, so check its steps, documents and any fees with the municipality and the Australian Embassy in Athens well before you book.
journey.reaction: Good, the legal side is up front and not left to the end. 'Well before you book' is the right order of things.

journey.section: Paros wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: "Not published" means the venue does not state the detail.
journey.reaction: I appreciate being told what it means rather than guessing. The table fits better than the last one did, though I still had to slide it on the iPad, and most of the capacity column is 'Not published'.

journey.quote: Anything this guide marks "Not published", from capacity to curfew, needs an answer in writing before you commit, so [talk to a Wedded Advisor about your shortlist]
journey.reaction: In writing, before we commit. Yes. Though this time it says the answer is needed, not who gets it. Is that my daughter's job, or the Advisor's?

journey.quote: Arriving by boat at the dock is the detail guests will remember.
journey.reaction: Lovely for the young ones. I'm picturing my mother and her walking frame getting off a boat onto a dock. It needs to say the road is there for people like her, and it does say guests can come by road, so I'll let it pass, but my first thought was worry.

journey.quote: The farm limits itself to 10 weddings a year, and its team is on site to oversee every supplier for the whole rental period.
journey.reaction: That's the sort of thing I'd read out to my husband. Only ten a year and their own people watching the suppliers. Someone accountable on the day.

journey.section: Pyrgaki Hotel, above the gulf of Parikia
journey.quote: Ask for current terms, as the page dates from 2020.
journey.reaction: Honest. I'd rather be told the information is old than find out after paying a deposit.

journey.section: The Secret View at Fladakia Estate, above Golden Beach
journey.quote: Rooms: None on site; guests stay in nearby hotels, and the venue says it is happy to organise shuttles.
journey.reaction: Shuttles they organise themselves. That answers a question I'd have asked. I'd want to know if the shuttle can take a walking frame, but it's a start.

journey.section: The Secret View at Fladakia Estate, above Golden Beach
journey.quote: House rules are published: loud music stops at 2am, out of respect for the local villages, with a quieter after-party (an acoustic band, for example) possible.
journey.reaction: Practical and considerate. This is what a contract would say, and it's good to know before rather than after.

Every venue seems to have a chapel, and not one word about whether you can get to it without steps. 'Perched', 'on the hills', 'high above the bay'. Those all mean stairs to me, and the article never once raises access for older guests at a venue.

journey.quote: All notarial services need an appointment, Monday to Friday, 9am to 12.30pm, though apostille and CNI documents can be sent by post.
journey.reaction: Clear, and nicely broken up. I still don't know who actually does this paperwork in the end: the couple, the venue or the Advisor.

journey.quote: Expect crowds and heat at the busy ports from May to October, and stairs to carry luggage up and down.
journey.reaction: Thank you for saying it. Stairs and luggage is exactly what I'd worry about for Mum, and it tells me she should fly, not take the ferry.

journey.quote: Build that into the arrival day for older guests.
journey.reaction: Someone thought about people my mother's age without making me feel fussy. I liked that.

journey.quote: Smartraveller suggests arranging a coach or taxi in advance.
journey.reaction: Fine, but who arranges it? I'm not having an 88-year-old standing in a taxi queue at the port. I'd want someone to say 'we organise the transfers'.

journey.quote: For a summer date, plan shade, a later ceremony and a covered fallback.
journey.reaction: Sensible, government advice behind it, and dated. Still nothing on travel or medical insurance, which is the first thing I'd sort for Mum in that heat.

journey.quote: Ask every venue on your shortlist these questions, and get the answers in writing:
journey.reaction: A good list, and I'll print it. But there's no line for access: can an older guest get from the room to the chapel and the reception without steps? That's the question I'd add in pen.

journey.section: Shortlist your Paros venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and every inclusion is confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: One person, AUD, fee in writing. That's the paragraph my husband needs to see. I'd still want a phone call before a cent changes hands.

unanswered_questions: Which of these venues have step-free or level access between rooms, chapel and reception, for a guest with a walking frame?
Who arranges private transfers from the airport or port for older guests, and can the venue shuttles take a walking frame?
What travel or medical insurance should older guests carry for a summer wedding in Greece?
Who prepares and lodges the legal paperwork, such as the CNI: the couple, the venue or the Wedded Advisor?
Who gets the 'Not published' answers in writing from the venue: my daughter or the Wedded Advisor?
Who reads a venue contract in Greek and in euros, and is the venue deposit protected?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong at 2am Paros time?
Is the first step a phone call with the Wedded Advisor, before anything is booked or paid?
would_share_with: My husband, with the closing section (fee in writing, AUD) and the Petra Farm line about ten weddings a year and their team on site
My daughter, with the booking checklist (I'll add the access question) and The Secret View house rules
My sister, who is looking after Mum on the trip, with the 'Getting to Paros' stairs and luggage line and the heat and wildfire advice

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
cta_reaction.why: A named person, Australian time, AUD and the fee in writing tick most of my boxes. I'd click if it said plainly that a real person rings me first, before anything is booked, and that they'll check which venues my mother can actually get around.

top_3_changes: Add a 'Step-free access' line to the booking checklist (and ideally to the per-venue bullets as 'Not published'), and note that hillside and hilltop venues (Petra Farm, Pyrgaki, Villa Mira, The Secret View) may mean steps for guests with limited mobility.

In 'Getting to Paros', after the Smartraveller coach or taxi line, say who can organise transfers for older guests; and in 'When to marry', add one line on travel and medical insurance for a summer date.
Say in one plain sentence who gets the 'Not published' answers in writing and who handles the legal paperwork in practice (the couple, the venue or the Wedded Advisor).

checks.check: Every journey point and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, practical, reads top to bottom on an iPad)
No invented brand facts; missing business details listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments, image slots and VERIFY markers treated as invisible
Title, deferred business details, sourcing lines and unprinted prices not raised as must-fix, per orchestrator

Journey types limited to the allowed enum; turn_offs_found empty because no persona turn-off was genuinely triggered (no slang, short paragraphs, responsibility covered by the Wedded Advisor and in-writing lines; deposits and contracts are deferred business details)

open_questions.question: For this persona the Paros draft does well on practical travel (port stairs, older guests on arrival day, venue shuttles, Petra Farm's on-site team). The main gap is accessibility: no venue mentions step-free access and the booking checklist omits it. Treat the checklist line as should-fix? Insurance and organised transfers are lower. Deposit, contract language and on-the-day contact are deferred business details.

assumptions: Margaret reads the whole article on an iPad because her daughter sent it, and her own mother uses a walking frame (per voice samples).
Prices are deliberately not printed, so their absence was not raised.
